title: Security — OAuth2/PKCE, JWT, OWASP
exp: Be fluent in auth code + PKCE, JWT validation claims, and the OWASP issues that hit .NET APIs.
pts: Auth Code + PKCE for public clients; exchange code for tokens server-side or with verifier.
Validate JWT: issuer, audience, lifetime, signature (and preferably `typ`).
OWASP: parameterized SQL/EF, encode XSS, antiforgery for cookies, secrets in Key Vault, DTOs against over-posting.
Password hashing: Identity / PBKDF2 / Argon2 / bcrypt — never raw SHA.
AuthN vs AuthZ: who you are vs what you can do (policies/roles).

r: Deep dive into Day 9 runtime execution mechanics and threading constraints.
Focus on zero-allocation and lock-free patterns where applicable.
High concurrency contention or unexpected resource exhaustion under load.
Implement resilient backpressure, retries, and circuit breakers.
Balancing low latency, developer ergonomics, and system consistency.
Always state operational cost and complexity trade-offs.

qa.q: Explain Authorization Code flow with PKCE.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Client sends authorize request with code_challenge; user authenticates; AS returns a code; client exchanges code + code_verifier for tokens. PKCE stops intercepted codes from being redeemed by attackers who lack the verifier.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Operating Explain Authorization Code flow with PKCE. at scale requires understanding the runtime lifecycle, memory allocations, and underlying execution constraints. The underlying framework or storage engine optimizes execution when contracts are explicitly preserved.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Un-handled edge cases in Explain Authorization Code flow with PKCE. under high concurrent traffic can lead to performance degradation, unhandled exceptions, or unexpected memory growth. Always enforce defensive validation and error handling.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Choosing this implementation approach balances developer velocity and system performance. Senior engineers evaluate latency, operational overhead, and maintenance costs before committing.

qa.q: Name five OWASP mitigations you'd apply to an ASP.NET API.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Parameterized queries/EF; output encoding; CSRF protection for cookie sessions; secrets out of source; least-privilege authZ policies; strict DTOs; security headers; dependency scanning.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.
